title: Burst Reservoir: soft-commit leasing, per-minute metering, and prorated invoice smoothing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a burst reservoir (soft-commit) mechanism for Dedicated fleets to allow short-lived temporary boosts without immediate hard overage charges. The feature will allocate a transient 'reservoir' of headroom that tenants can borrow from for minute-scale spikes. Borrowed capacity will be metered per-minute, reconciled against committed capacity, and invoiced with an automated smoothing policy that prorates and, in qualifying cases, applies partial credits to avoid one-off invoice surprises. Includes operator controls to reclaim, quarantine, or extend reservoirs, and UI signals for cost/latency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Reservoir allocation API supports create/update/delete with tenant, size (vCPU/GPU-equivalent), TTL and priority tags
Per-tenant per-minute metering pipeline emits usage events to billing with <=30s delay under normal load
Billing reconciler applies prorated charges and a configurable grace window (default 10 minutes) before hard overage billing
Operator console shows active reservoirs, reclaimed events, and predicted exhaustion ETA with confidence bands
Canary rollout on a single dedicated fleet with non-critical customers for 72 hours without >1% error rate regression
design_notes: We introduce a separate "reservoir manager" component that sits between router and scheduler: it consults soft-commit quotas before applying backpressure. Credits are 'decaying' tokens: they reduce as time passes or as usage is consumed. Policy: if a tenant is within their committed capacity, no reservoir is touched. If they exceed, requests first consume reservoir tokens (minute-buckets) then fall back to configured surge lanes or throttles. Billing side uses an additive ledger where reservoir usage is labeled 'transient' and gets an extra metadata field for reconciliation. We chose minute-level granularity to balance billing accuracy and pipeline overhead.
implementation_plan: 1) Spike: prototype meter and tiny allocator (2w). 2) Core: implement reservoir manager and allocation API, integrate with router (3w). 3) Billing: extend meter consumer and reconciliation rules (2w). 4) UI/ops: console table + operator reclaim actions (1w). 5) Canary & rollouts + postmortem (2w).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal canary on staging fleets (1 week). Phase 2: Gradual canary to 5 dedicated fleets (2 weeks) with observability enabled. Phase 3: Open opt-in for high-usage tenants (2 weeks) with customer notifications. Phase 4: Default-on for new dedicated tenants after 30 days and opt-out for existing customers once support runs workshops.
tasks: Spike: simulate per-minute metering and downstream cost estimate
API: add /reservoirs endpoints and RBAC checks
Router: consult reservoir manager before hitting surge lanes
Billing: tag ledger entries and implement grace window reconciliation
E2E tests: billing accuracy and long-run leakage tests
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Metering pipeline delay causes inaccurate invoices -> Mitigation: circuit-breaker to pause reservoir consumption if lag > 2 minutes and trigger alert
Risk: Tenants abuse reservoirs causing noisy neighbors -> Mitigation: per-tenant burst rate limits and adaptive scoring that lowers reservoir priority on repeated abuse
Risk: Complex billing semantics confuse customers -> Mitigation: clear UI breakdown, pre-billing emails, and opt-in during initial rollout
security_considerations: Reservoir allocation API must require tenant-scoped permissions and audit logs. Billing metadata contains tenant usage labels; ensure billing pipeline uses KMS-encrypted storage for ledgers and redact PII. Security review requested before Phase 2.
customer_communications: Draft notification for early adopters: 'We're introducing a temporary burst reservoir to reduce outage risk and smooth short spikes. You'll receive transparent line items for transient usage and provisional credits if spike is below SLA thresholds.'
postmortem_plan: If we observe >2% of invoices disputed in first 30 days, pause automatic charge application, run full reconciliation, and issue manual credits while onboarding customers to new billing docs.
